subject: P0: Central-2 persistent 5xx + timeouts — request for cross-region drain and customer credit
messages:
From: Jake Porter <jake.porter@cloudretail.com>
To: dylan_brooks@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 17 Sep 2028 08:12:05 -0700
Subject: Production timeouts and 5xx from central-2.az — urgent

Hi Dylan —

We're seeing a steady surge of 500s and checkout timeouts starting ~07:50 PDT this morning. Error rate on our payment microservice has jumped from ~0.2% to 8.6% and client-side retries have ballooned. This is impacting conversion on our main checkout funnel (pageviews -> checkout started down ~12% over last 20m).

Sample request ids: rq_11a2b, rq_11a2c, rq_11a2d. Host pattern indicates Central-2 AZ c2-3.* (we're routing to this AZ by geo affinity).

Can you confirm whether this is an infrastructure degradation, or something we need to route away from? We need an ETA — this is a P0 for us.

Thanks,
Jake
Jake Porter
Head of Platform Reliability, CloudRetail
From: dylan_brooks@redwood.com
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, hannah_schmitt@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, sean_gallagher@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 17 Sep 2028 08:19:42 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production timeouts and 5xx from central-2.az — urgent

Team — FYI customer CloudRetail reporting rising 5xxs and retries originating in Central-2 AZ (c2-3 hosts). Initial Kibana tail attached (kibana-error-snippet.txt).

Quick summary of evidence so far:
- Error signature looks like backend KV cache timeouts -> 502/504 conversion to user 500s.
- Traffic surge pattern is uneven: a small % of requests amplify due to client retries and bucketed routing.
- Central-1 is healthy; Central-2 shows elevated queue depths on the kernel and modest GPU contention on a subset of pools.

I'd like to request an immediate geo-drain of CloudRetail traffic away from Central-2 to Central-1 (manual steering + rps cap) while infra teams investigate. Additionally, the customer is asking for a one-time credit and a postmortem. I need:
- approval to execute geo-drain now (Vanessa / Hannah)
- approval for preliminary customer credit (Marissa) — propose 10% of last bill as a good-faith one-time credit until postmortem final
- James/ops (cc'd in incident bridge) to push routing change and confirm capacity headroom in Central-1

I'll open an exec bridge now and keep Jake updated with a 30m ETA for the first mitigation step.

-Dylan

On Sun, Sep 17, 2028 at 08:12 AM Jake Porter <jake.porter@cloudretail.com> wrote:
> We're seeing a steady surge of 500s and checkout timeouts starting ~07:50 PDT this morning...
From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
To: dylan_brooks@redwood.com, hannah_schmitt@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: sean_gallagher@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 17 Sep 2028 08:28:11 -07:00
Subject: Re: P0: Central-2 persistent 5xx + timeouts — request for cross-region drain and customer credit

Thanks Dylan — I approve immediate geo-drain for CloudRetail to Central-1 in stepped increments. Before we flip more than 25% of traffic, Ops needs to confirm Central-1 spare headroom and also that prefix/KV cache warming won't cause a worse spike.

Action items I authorize now:
- Ops: enact 25% initial divert, monitor latency & error delta for 5m windows (attach traffic-metrics-15m.png).
- SRE (Hannah): instrument temporary request-level rate limiting for client retries to avoid amplification.
- Ops: prepare rollback plan if Central-1 error rate rises beyond +3x baseline.

Marissa — can you greenlight a provisional 10% one-time credit pending final postmortem? We should avoid long approval loops in a live incident.

Vanessa
From: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
To: ops-team@redwood.com, dylan_brooks@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 17 Sep 2028 08:41:02 -07:00
Subject: Re: P0: Central-2 persistent 5xx + timeouts — ops actions initiated

On it — initiating stepped divert now. Command summary:
- route adjust: divert 25% traffic for customer CR-3491 from central-2 -> central-1 at 08:41:24 PDT
- KV cache pre-warm job kicked (short-lived filling of hot prefixes)
- temporary retry-limit set: client_retry_cap = 2 for CloudRetail customer token ranges

First 5min window looks promising: 5xx rate down from 8.6% -> 2.1%; median latency in Central-1 increased from 42ms -> 65ms (within SLO but trending). Pushing timeline-snapshot.png to the drive link for the exec summary.

On Sun, Sep 17, 2028 at 08:28 AM Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com> wrote:
> Thanks Dylan — I approve immediate geo-drain for CloudRetail to Central-1 in stepped increments...
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: dylan_brooks@redwood.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
Cc: sean_gallagher@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 17 Sep 2028 09:05:30 -07:00
Subject: Re: P0: Central-2 persistent 5xx + timeouts — credit approval

Approve provisional credit: one-time 10% of the monthly bill for CloudRetail (applied to the next invoice) pending a full postmortem and final customer remediation plan. Finance to apply after postmortem acceptance.

Also: please capture the following for the exec postmortem doc —
- timeline + triggers (when divert started, when error drops observed)
- root-cause hypothesis: localized KV timeouts under burst + retry amplification at the app layer
- mitigation steps taken: geo-drain, retry caps, KV pre-warm
- next steps: longer-term cache sharding review + routing affinity changes for high-retry customers

I'll draft an executive note for the leadership team and include the timeline snapshot. Thanks all for the quick turnaround.

Marissa
VP, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
From: Jake Porter <jake.porter@cloudretail.com>
To: dylan_brooks@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 17 Sep 2028 11:05:30 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production timeouts and 5xx from central-2.az — urgent

Dylan —

Thanks for the rapid response and the 25% divert. We're seeing conversion return toward normal and page-level errors dropping. We appreciate the provisional credit offer and the plan for a postmortem. Please include the timeline and root-cause analysis when available; our CTO would like a short write-up for her SLT.

Also, can you confirm whether there will be any change to our SLA targets as a result of this event, or if the credit will be the only remediation?

Best,
Jake
